messages.subject: Multiple likelihoods for mesh models
parts:
Hi,

I am interested in modeling two responses, (i.e. wasting and maternal overweight and obese). I have tried reading on ways to manipulate more than one likelihood but i cant seem to get a feel on the way i would go about it.

Below is a code where i fitted only one response, but wondering how i would add the other response.


##--- Constructing the SPDE object
#Assumptions: Non Stationarity and Anisotropy

basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2,degree=2)

spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, 
                         alpha = 2,
                         B.tau = cbind(0, basis.T, basis.K*0),
                         B.kappa = cbind(0, basis.T*0, basis.K/2))

no.years <- length(unique(data.train$time))

#names.zzz <- "the covariates in my model"

# restructure my data

n = dim(data.train)[1]
N = 2*n

##two reponses am interested in modeling
y1 <- data.train$wasting
y2 <- data.train$maternal_overweight_obese

## Join them together
Y = matrix(NA, N, 2)
Y[1:n, 1] = y1
Y[1:n + n, 2] = y2

x = data.train[,names.zzz]

##--- Observation structure for estimation data
A.est =
  inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
                   loc=
                     as.matrix(coordinates.train[data.train$cluster_id,
                                                 c("long","lat")]),
                   group = data.train$time,
                   n.group = no.years
  )


##--- Observation structure for validation data
A.val =
  inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
                   loc=
                     as.matrix(coordinates.val[data.val$cluster_id,
                                               c("long","lat")]),
                   group = data.val$time,
                   n.group = no.years
  )

i_year <- 3 #prediction year

##--- Observation structure for field prediction
A.pred =
  inla.spde.make.A(mesh ,group = i_year, n.group = no.years
  )

field.indices =
  inla.spde.make.index("field",
                       n.spde = mesh$n,
                       n.group=no.years
  )


stack.est =
  inla.stack(data=list(y = data.train$y),
             A=list(A.est, 1),
             effects=
               list(c(field.indices,
                      list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(data.train[,names.zzz])),
             tag="est")

stack.val =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
             A=list(A.val, 1),
             effects=
               list(c(field.indices,
                      list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(data.val[,names.zzz])),
             tag="val")


scaled.mesh.loc =
  list(long=(rep(scale(mesh$loc[,1],
                       mean.covariates["long"],
                       sd.covariates["long"]),
                 no.years
  )),
  lat=(rep(scale(mesh$loc[,2],
                 mean.covariates["lat"],
                 sd.covariates["lat"]),
           no.years
  )))

stack.pred =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
             A=list(A.pred),
             effects=
               list(c(field.indices,
                      scaled.mesh.loc,
                      list(Intercept=1))),
             tag="pred")

stack = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.val, stack.pred)
str(stack)


ntrials = c(df.final.03.train1$N,data.val$N,rep(NA,mesh$n))

results = 
  inla(formula = f,
       data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde = spde),
       family = "binomial", 
       Ntrials = ntrials,
       control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),link = 1,compute=TRUE),
       control.compute = list(cpo=T,dic=TRUE),
       keep = FALSE,
       verbose = TRUE)

Thomas.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multiple likelihoods for mesh models
parts:
Hi,

The main issue is that you are not building the data stack accounting
for multiple likelihood. You can follow examples in the last Chapter of
the INLA book or in Chapter 3 of the current spde-tutorial version.

In advance you have to specify two columns data as something like this

stack.est1 = inla.stack(
data = list(y=cbind(data.train$wasting,NA),trials=data.train$N),
...)
stack.est2 = inla.stack(
data =
list(y=cbind(NA,data.train$maternal_overweight_obese),trials=data.train$N),
...)

So you have one stack for each outcome with the first in the first
column of data and the second in the second along with the number of
trials. These two data stack need to be join to use in inla().

Elias
